gaps.sentence: If the pilot ___ the storm, we would have landed on time.
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition takes the past perfect: had avoided.

gaps.sentence: If he ___ so stubborn, we would have reached an agreement by now.
gaps.hint: present cause with a result up to now
gaps.explanation: An unreal present cause can produce a result reaching into the past; formally 'were' is used: were not.

gaps.sentence: If you ___ a red light, you must stop.
gaps.explanation: General rules use the present simple in the if-clause: come to.

gaps.sentence: If I had known you were coming, I ___ a cake.
gaps.hint: unreal past result, would have participle
gaps.explanation: The result of an unreal past condition is 'would have' plus the past participle: would have baked.

gaps.sentence: They would have won the match if their best player ___ injured.
gaps.hint: unreal past needs the past perfect
gaps.explanation: The unreal past condition requires the past perfect: had not been.

gaps.sentence: You can stay out late as long as you ___ me a text when you arrive.
gaps.hint: as long as plus present simple
gaps.explanation: 'As long as' introduces the condition and takes the present simple: send.

gaps.sentence: I will tell her the news when I ___ her at the party.
gaps.hint: when clauses take present for future
gaps.explanation: Time clauses with future meaning use the present simple, not 'will': see.

gaps.sentence: She keeps a spare key at her mother's in case she ___ herself out.
gaps.hint: a precaution, in case plus present
gaps.explanation: 'In case' clauses use the present simple for possible future problems: locks.
